items.title: The game of basketball is about shot efficiency & shot quantity
items.author: Hoop Informatics
items.body_excerpt:
The game of basketball is about shot efficiency & shot quantity 

One of my favorite team stats to track who is winning the possession battle is true shot +/-

This chart shows the Toronto Raptors have been taking 12.4 more shots per game than their opponents this season.

images.alt:
A table titled "Who's Getting More Shots Up?" showing true shot attempts per game for and against for all 30 NBA teams through Oct. 28, 2026. True shot attempts (TSA) equal field goal attempts plus 0.44 times free throw attempts. Each row shows the team's logo, name, games played, and its own FGA, FTA and TSA, then the same three stats for its opponents. The last column, +/-, is TSA for minus TSA against. It is shaded teal for positive values and magenta for negative ones, and the color gets stronger the bigger the gap. Teams are sorted by +/-.

Toronto Raptors lead by a wide margin at +12.4, with 107.6 TSA for and 95.3 against. Orlando Magic are last at -9.5, with 96.2 for and 105.6 against.

Full order: Toronto Raptors +12.4, San Antonio Spurs +6.5, Atlanta Hawks +6.1, Portland Trail Blazers +5.2, Golden State Warriors +4.8, Minnesota Timberwolves +4.3, New York Knicks +3.8, Boston Celtics +3.3, Memphis Grizzlies +2.7, Oklahoma City Thunder +2.7, Brooklyn Nets +2.6, Philadelphia 76ers +1.8, Charlotte Hornets +1.1, Miami Heat +0.6, New Orleans Pelicans +0.6, Indiana Pacers -0.7, Sacramento Kings -1.5, Utah Jazz -1.9, Denver Nuggets -2.2, Cleveland Cavaliers -2.5, Detroit Pistons -2.6, Milwaukee Bucks -3.1, Los Angeles Lakers -3.7, Houston Rockets -4.3, Chicago Bulls -4.5, Phoenix Suns -4.6, Dallas Mavericks -4.7, Los Angeles Clippers -4.9, Washington Wizards -7.2, Orlando Magic -9.5.

Teams have played 3 to 5 games, so samples are small. Data: Basketball Reference. Viz: @Hoopinformatics.com on Bluesky.
